newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cen.bank head confirms Ukraine has currency band.
newsitem.headline: Cen.bank head confirms Ukraine has currency band.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko on Tuesday confirmed the former Soviet republic had implemented a currency corridor, or trading band, of 1.70 to 1.90 hryvnias to the dollar since 1995.
"The official currency corridor for the hryvnia is 1.70-1.90 to the dollar," Yushchenko told entrepreneurs at an "Investment Window for Ukraine" conference in Frankfurt.

Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, whose resignation is expected to be accepted this week, in May cast doubt on the existence of the trading band -- formally announced in April by Serhiy Tyhypko, deputy prime minister in charge of reforms.
But Yushchenko told delegates the central bank had intervened on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange (UICE) since 1995 to keep the hryvnia within the band's parameters.
The hryvnia was unchanged at 1.8570 on Tuesday on the UICE.
